title: Rebecca at the well (Genesis 24)
hookLine: a servant prays for a sign and a young woman waters ten camels
last: THE TWO OF THEM WENT ON TOGETHER.

lines: SENT BACK TO THE OLD COUNTRY.
cards: Genesis twenty-four is a long chapter, and its hero doesn't even get a name. He's the elder servant of Abraham's house, the one in charge of everything.
Abraham, very old now, sends him back to the old country in Mesopotamia to find a wife for Isaac among his own relatives. The servant loads ten camels with gifts and makes the long trip.
He arrives at evening, at a well outside the city, at the hour the women come out to draw water. And he has no idea what he's looking for. So he does the only thing he can think of.

teach.h: HE PRAYS FOR A GENEROUS HEART.
teach.b: First, the prayer. He asks God to show kindness to his master, and he names a sign.
Let the young woman to whom I say, let down thy pitcher that I may drink, be the one who answers: drink, and I'll give thy camels drink also. Notice what he's asking for. Not beauty, not wealth.
A generous heart. Second, the answer.
Before he's even finished praying, Rebecca comes out with a pitcher on her shoulder. He runs to her and asks for a little water, and she lowers the jar and gives it to him.
Then, in the Douay-Rheims: "And when he had drunk, she said: I will draw water for thy camels also, till they all drink." Third, the size of that offer. Ten camels after a desert journey.

She runs back and forth to the well, emptying her jar into the trough, again and again, until every one is done. Nobody asked her to. That's the sign: not that she gave water, but that she did more than she was asked.
The servant watches in silence, wondering. Fourth, the choice.

teach.h: THEY ASK HER: WILL YOU GO?
teach.b: When the family discusses it, they end by asking her.
Will you go with this man? And Rebecca says, in the Douay-Rheims: "I will go." Just that.
Another person leaving home for a land she hasn't seen, like Abraham before her. The servant bows to the ground and thanks God, whose kindness, he says, has led him the whole way.

how: Catholics remember Rebecca among the matriarchs of faith, and Genesis 24 is one of the Old Testament readings the Church offers for weddings.

o: the water drawn from a well at evening
a bride's promise to leave her home

games.q: what's inside the well story — tap the pairs.

s: the servant asks God for a beautiful wife for Isaac
he asks for a sign of a generous heart: the one who offers water to his camels too.
Rebecca's family asks her whether she will go
the servant in Genesis 24 is named in the chapter
he's only called Abraham's servant. later tradition often calls him Eliezer.

games.q: you're at the well with your water jar. a tired stranger with ten camels asks for a little water. what do you do?
o: give him a drink and go home.
give him a drink, then water all ten camels.
point him to the trough and let him do it himself.
games.why: "I will draw water for thy camels also, till they all drink." she did more than she was asked, and that was the sign.

practice: Think of one request you know is coming, a file for a coworker, help with homework, milk from the store, and picture Rebecca at the trough, jar after jar.
What's the camels-too version: sending the file and offering to look it over, picking up the milk and the thing they forgot? If you pray, ask for a generous heart like hers.

wordCard.voice: Chesed, kindness, faithful love: what the servant prayed for, and what Rebecca showed when she watered all ten of his camels. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: kindness, faithful love. the servant asks God to show it to his master, and thanks God for it at the end.

carryVoice: Your line: the camels too. A generous heart was the whole sign. Day three hundred fifty-three, done.
